findings.claim: The minimum of 13 verbs is an unexplained constant equal to the current number of verbs. If a verb is removed on purpose, runReview routes 12 verbs and the test fails with the message 'the parse found nothing it should'. That message is wrong in that case: the parse worked and a verb was removed. The check is meant to catch a parse that found nothing, and a minimum of 1, or a comment that says the number tracks the current verb count, would state that intent without misleading the next maintainer.

findings.claim: The CHANGELOG part of the check only looks for the words 'review <verb>' anywhere in the whole file. Because of this, a new verb whose name already appears after 'review ' somewhere in CHANGELOG.md (in any entry, any section, including Removed or released sections) passes even though it has no entry of its own. The same mistake that put review findings out of the CHANGELOG could then reach a PR unseen. Checking only the '## Unreleased' section, or only entry-leading forms like 'labdrian review <verb>', would make the check tighter. The design records this as accepted risk R2, but the gap still exists in the CHANGELOG part.

findings.claim: There are two more places that list the review verbs, and the class check covers neither: the 'review requires a verb: ...' message and the 'unknown verb ... (expected ...)' message in runReview. If someone adds a new case "x" with its docs in all five documented places but leaves it out of these two messages, every test still passes, and the CLI's own refusal text no longer names a routed verb. This is the same class of error the commit is meant to close: a verb missing from a place that lists the verbs. The design rejected these messages as the source of the verb list, but not as places to check.

findings.claim: To find the routed switch, the code accepts any switch on an index of 'args' (args[i] for any i) inside runReview, and stops looking inside that switch once it matches. It does not check that the index is the literal 0. If a later edit adds a switch on args[1] or args[len(args)-1] earlier in runReview, for example to check flags, the cases of that switch are collected as routed verbs. The test then demands docs for strings like '--base', while still passing the 13-verb minimum. The failure is loud, so it is not a false pass.
